newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian parties poised for early general election.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parties poised for early general election.

text.p: The following is a list of Albania's main political parties and their strength in the 140-member parliament when it was dissolved on May 16 ahead of early general elections on Sunday.
Democratic Party.....122 seats
Socialist Party............. 9
Republican Party......... 3
Human Rights Union Party.......... 3
National Front Party..... 2
Independent.. 1
A national unity coalition government was formed on March 11 following the outbreak of violence across large swathes of the Balkan state. The following parties make up the coalition.

DEMOCRATIC PARTY -- right-leaning, was formed as Albania's main opposition party after a popular revolt swept the reform communist successors to Stalinist dictator Enver Hoxha from power in 1990. It formed the first non-communist government in 1992 and won 122 out of 140 seats in parliament in a disputed general election in May last year.
Four centre-right and right-wing parties have split from the Democrats, partly over what they considered to be President Sali Berisha's authoritarian style of government.

SOCIALIST PARTY -- successor of the communist Party of Labour which ruled Albania for 45 years. The party officially ditched Marxism last year. Its leader, Fatos Nano, was jailed in 1994 on corruption charges after a trial some Western governments considered suspect. He was released last March.
SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC PARTY -- centre-left grouping led by Skender Gjinushi and campaigning in alliance with the Socialists for the upcoming election.
REPUBLICAN PARTY -- rightist, nationalist party led by Sabri Godo which has created an electoral alliance with other right-wing parties called the Albanian United Right.
NATIONAL FRONT PARTY -- an extreme rightist party led by Abaz Ermenji, allied with the Republicans.
DEMOCRATIC ALLIANCE PARTY -- centre-right grouping founded in 1992 by politicians who split from the Democratic Party. It is led by Neritan Ceka.
HUMAN RIGHTS UNION PARTY -- ethnic Greek party formed in 1992. It says it represents the thousands of ethnic Greeks who mainly live in southern Albania bordering Greece.

SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC UNION PARTY -- centre-left party, split from the Social Democratic Party in 1994 and led by Teodor Laco, a former minister of culture. The party has formed an electoral pact with the Democrats, called the Union for Democracy, which includes royalists and Christian Democrats.

MOVEMENT OF LEGALITY -- royalist party that has organised a referendum to take place on the same day as the June 29 election, asking voters whether they favour a constitutional monarchy or a continued republic. Most analysts believe Albanians will vote to keep the republic.
CHRISTIAN DEMOCRATIC PARTY -- rightist grouping with a small following.
There are 22 other smaller parties contesting the two-round election being held on June 29 and July 6.
